blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **придёт** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. future: я приду́ · ты придёшь · он придёт · мы придём · вы придёте · они приду́т. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: He is sure that he will come.
exercises.context: **при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **вышли** is the past tense (plural) of **выйти** (to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **выходить**. past: он вы́шел · она вы́шла · оно вы́шло · они вы́шли. — Wiktionary, «выйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **провёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **провести**: to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.; to carry out, to carry through, to realize, to put into practice, to conduct; to pass over, to run over.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Проводить — провести — to lead through, to spend (time), to lay (a road). Note the expression: "проводить время" — to spend the time.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Did you have a good time in Vegas?
exercises.context: The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. (DLI, Lesson 79)

exercises.why: **переведите** is the imperative (вы, plural or polite) of **перевести** (to lead, to convey, to transfer, to move, to shift, to transmit, to switch; to translate, to interpret [with с (s, + genitive) ‘from a language’ and на (na, + accusative) ‘into a language’]) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переводить**. imperative: переведи́ · переведи́те. — Wiktionary, «перевести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  «переводить — перевести — to lead over; to transfer, to translate. Note the following meanings:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я перевёл детей через дорогу.» (to lead over (across)) — DLI, Lesson 79. «Меня перевели в другой полк.» (to transfer) — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **пришли** is the past tense (plural) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **отойти** (the infinitive) (to go away, to go aside, to move away, to move aside; (military) to withdraw, to fall back) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отходить**. — Wiktionary, «отойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  Compare: «Я съезжу на вокзал и узнаю, когда отходит поезд.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **разведём** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **развести** (to take along, to bring; to conduct) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **разводить**. future: я разведу́ · ты разведёшь · он разведёт · мы разведём · вы разведёте · они разведу́т. — Wiktionary, «развести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **зашли** is the past tense (plural) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. past: он зашёл · она зашла́ · оно зашло́ · они зашли́. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I want you to come over.
exercises.context: **за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **принесла** is the past tense (feminine) of **принести** (to bring (by foot), to fetch (transitive) to transport toward someone/somewhere); to yield, to bear) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приносить**. past: он принёс · она принесла́ · оно принесло́ · они принесли́. — Wiktionary, «принести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «приносить — принести — to bring (on foot).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **наведите** is the imperative (вы, plural or polite) of **навести** (to direct (at), to aim (at), to point (at); to cover, to coat, to apply) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **наводить**. imperative: наведи́ · наведи́те. — Wiktionary, «навести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. Prepositional phrases: в/на + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **на-** — Movement onto the surface of an object; only formed from multidirectional verb of motion Example: Туча наползла на солнце. — A cloud crept onto the sun. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **пролетели** is the past tense (plural) of **пролететь** (to fly (by, past, through), to fly (over); to overfly, to overshoot) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **пролетать**. past: он пролете́л · она пролете́ла · оно пролете́ло · они пролете́ли. — Wiktionary, «пролететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **ушли** is the past tense (plural) of **уйти** (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **уходить**. past: он ушёл · она ушла́ · оно ушло́ · они ушли́. — Wiktionary, «уйти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **заводит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **заводить** (to take, to bring, to lead; to get, to procure, to acquire, to buy) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **завести**. present: я завожу́ · ты заво́дишь · он заво́дит · мы заво́дим · вы заво́дите · они заво́дят. — Wiktionary, «заводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **ввёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **ввести** (to introduce; to bring in, to usher in) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вводить**. past: он ввёл · она ввела́ · оно ввело́ · они ввели́. — Wiktionary, «ввести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **подводить** (the infinitive) (to bring closer; to place (under)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **подвести**. — Wiktionary, «подводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**под-, подо-** — Approach. Antonym: от- Example: Он подошёл к девушке, чтобы спросить её номер. — He approached the girl to ask for her number. Prepositional phrases: к + dat.; до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix под- denote approaching to an object, a place or a person and require the preposition к + dative case: Я подхожу к столу. Рядовой подходит к сержанту. Мы подъезжаем к городу.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I don't want to let her down.
exercises.context: **под-, подо-** — Approach. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **уплывать** (the infinitive) (to swim away; to sail away) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уплыть**. — Wiktionary, «уплывать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: **у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **обошли** is the past tense (plural) of **обойти** (to go around, to bypass (to pass by going around); to walk through, to wander around, to go around, to tour, to go to (many places in an area)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **обходить**. past: он обошёл · она обошла́ · оно обошло́ · они обошли́. — Wiktionary, «обойти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**о-, об-, обо-** — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place Example: Девочка обошла лужу. — The little girl walked around the puddle. Я обхожу все магазины в центре. — I'm going around to all the stores in the mall. Prepositional phrases: вокруг + gen.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "об-" indicates a motion around a place and may mean: a) Circling a place. The verb is followed by the preposition вокруг + Gen.: Самолёт облетел вокруг аэродрома. Я хочу объехать вокруг озера. b) Making a detour. No preposition is used; the verb is followed by the Accusative case: Мы объехали это место. Противник обошёл наш город. c) Making the rounds of … or going all over … No preposition is used; the verb is followed by the Accusative case: Я обошёл все магазины. — I made the rounds of all the stores. Я обошёл весь город. — I walked all over town.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: We have walked all around the lake.
exercises.context: **о-, об-, обо-** — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place Example: Девочка обошла лужу. — The little girl walked around the puddle. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))
